unit.title: Cohésion de haut vol
unit.goal: Éviter les répétitions grâce à l'ellipse et à la substitution, et employer les collocations soutenues du niveau C2.

lesson.text: Un anglophone déteste se répéter. À [[Will it rain tomorrow?]], il ne répond pas [[Yes, I think it will rain tomorrow]] mais simplement [[I think so]]. C'est l'**ellipse** (on supprime) et la **substitution** (on remplace par un petit mot). Ajoute quelques **collocations** de haut niveau ([[pose a threat]], [[bear in mind]]…) et ton anglais sonnera aussi naturel que celui d'un éditorialiste.

lesson.title: So et not après les verbes d'opinion
lesson.text: Après [[think]], [[hope]], [[suppose]], [[expect]], [[guess]], [[believe]], [[imagine]] et [[I'm afraid]], **so** remplace toute une proposition positive, et **not** une proposition négative : [[Will we win? I hope so.]] (= j'espère que nous gagnerons) ; [[Will it rain? I hope not.]] (= j'espère qu'il ne pleuvra pas). [[I'm afraid so]] et [[I'm afraid not]] annoncent poliment une mauvaise nouvelle (« malheureusement oui / non »). Avec [[think]], [[believe]] et [[expect]], le négatif le plus naturel est [[I don't think so]] ([[I think not]] existe, mais sonne très soutenu).

lesson.title: Ne pas répéter : auxiliaire, to, do so, one / ones
lesson.text: **1. L'auxiliaire seul** remplace le verbe : [[I can't whistle, but my sister can.]] [[She said she would call, and she did.]] **2. [[to]] seul** remplace un infinitif déjà connu : [[Do you want to come? I'd love to.]] [[You can borrow my bike if you want to.]] **3. [[do so]]** (soutenu) remplace une action : [[Anyone who wishes to leave may do so now.]] **4. [[one]] / [[ones]]** remplace un nom **dénombrable** : [[I don't like this mug; I prefer the blue one.]] [[My mittens are wet, so I need dry ones.]]

Pièges de francophone : **1.** « Je pense que oui » = [[I think so]], jamais [[I think yes]] ; « J'espère que non » = [[I hope not]], jamais [[I hope no]] ni [[I don't hope so]]. **2.** « J'aimerais bien » en réponse = [[I'd love to]] : le **to** reste ! [[I'd love]] tout seul est incomplet. **3.** [[one]] ne remplace **jamais** un nom indénombrable : [[I prefer white bread to brown]], pas [[brown one]]. **4.** Au pluriel, c'est [[ones]] : des mitaines neuves = [[new ones]], pas [[new one]].

lesson.title: Les collocations de niveau C2
lesson.text: Une collocation, c'est un mariage de mots que les anglophones font **toujours** ensemble. Traduire mot à mot donne un résultat compréhensible… mais qui sonne faux. On dit [[pose a threat]] (pas [[make a threat]], qui veut dire « menacer quelqu'un »), [[draw a conclusion]] (pas [[take a conclusion]]), [[meet a deadline]] (pas [[respect a deadline]]), [[raise awareness]] (pas [[make awareness]]), [[shed light on]] (avec **on**, pas **in**). Attention : [[take into account]] se coupe souvent en deux : [[We took the weather into account.]]

head: Collocation
Sens
Exemple
rows: [[Plastic poses a threat to sea turtles.]]
[[Bear in mind that the store closes early.]]
[[It's too early to draw a conclusion.]]
[[He came to terms with the move.]]
[[Strike a balance between work and fun.]]
[[The letter sheds light on the mystery.]]
[[After an hour, we reached a compromise.]]
[[You run the risk of missing the bus.]]

items.en: Will the power come back tonight? I hope so.
items.fr: Le courant va-t-il revenir ce soir ? Je l'espère.

items.en: Did we win the contest? I'm afraid not.
items.fr: Avons-nous gagné le concours ? Malheureusement non.

items.en: I've never been skydiving, and I don't intend to.
items.fr: Je n'ai jamais fait de parachutisme, et je n'en ai pas l'intention.

items.en: This old laptop is slow, but the new one is amazing.
items.fr: Ce vieux portable est lent, mais le nouveau est incroyable.

items.en: Bear in mind that the last bus leaves at midnight.
items.fr: N'oublie pas que le dernier autobus part à minuit.

items.en: Raccoons pose a real threat to our garbage bins.
items.fr: Les ratons laveurs représentent une vraie menace pour nos poubelles.

lines.en: Do you think Mom suspects anything about the party?
lines.fr: Penses-tu que maman se doute de quelque chose pour la fête ?

lines.en: I don't think so. But bear in mind that she notices everything.
lines.fr: Je ne crois pas. Mais garde à l'esprit qu'elle remarque tout.

lines.en: Will Grandma be able to come?
I'm afraid not. Her flight was cancelled, but Uncle Samuel will.
lines.fr: Malheureusement non. Son vol a été annulé, mais oncle Samuel, lui, viendra.

lines.en: We have to strike a balance: a fun party, but not too noisy for the neighbours.
lines.fr: Il faut trouver le juste équilibre : une fête amusante, mais pas trop bruyante pour les voisins.

lines.en: Agreed. And the cake? The chocolate one or the lemon one?
lines.fr: D'accord. Et le gâteau ? Celui au chocolat ou celui au citron ?

lines.en: The chocolate one, obviously. Can you pick it up on Saturday?
lines.fr: Celui au chocolat, évidemment. Peux-tu aller le chercher samedi ?

lines.en: I'd love to, but I run the risk of eating it on the way home.
lines.fr: J'aimerais bien, mais je cours le risque de le manger sur le chemin du retour.

lesson.text: Le sais-tu ? Le mot [[ellipsis]] vient du grec et veut dire « omission, manque ». En anglais, c'est aussi le nom des trois points de suspension (…), ceux qu'on met justement quand on laisse une phrase… en suspens !

vocab.ex: Will the rink be open tomorrow? I hope so.

vocab.fr: malheureusement non (j'ai bien peur que non)
vocab.ex: Is there any cake left? I'm afraid not.

vocab.fr: malheureusement oui (j'ai bien peur que oui)
vocab.ex: Do we have to clean the garage? I'm afraid so.
Can the dog sleep on the couch? I suppose so.
Is Liam coming tonight? I don't think so.

vocab.fr: le faire (sans répéter le verbe, soutenu)
vocab.ex: If you want to ask a question, please do so now.
Invasive plants pose a threat to the park.

vocab.fr: garder à l'esprit, ne pas oublier
vocab.ex: Bear in mind that it gets dark early in December.
It's too soon to draw a conclusion.

vocab.fr: accepter, se faire à (une situation difficile)
vocab.ex: She finally came to terms with losing the final.

vocab.fr: se montrer indulgent envers (vu les circonstances)
vocab.ex: We should make allowances for Grandpa: he's very tired.
Did you take the traffic into account?
I stayed up late to meet the deadline.
It's hard to strike a balance between school and sports.
This photo sheds light on the mystery.
The students made posters to raise awareness of recycling.
My parents reached a compromise about the vacation.
If you leave now, you run the risk of getting stuck in traffic.

sentences.en: Will the library be open on Monday? I'm afraid not.
sentences.fr: La bibliothèque sera-t-elle ouverte lundi ? Malheureusement non.

sentences.en: Do you think Grandpa will like his gift? I think so.
sentences.fr: Penses-tu que grand-papa aimera son cadeau ? Je pense que oui.

sentences.en: We can leave early if you want to.
sentences.fr: On peut partir tôt si tu veux.

sentences.en: My brother can't whistle, but my sister can.
sentences.fr: Mon frère ne sait pas siffler, mais ma sœur, oui.

sentences.en: Anyone who wishes to leave early may do so after lunch.
sentences.fr: Ceux qui souhaitent partir tôt peuvent le faire après le dîner (repas du midi).

sentences.en: These boots are too small, so I need bigger ones.
sentences.fr: Ces bottes sont trop petites, alors il m'en faut des plus grandes.

sentences.en: Pollution poses a serious threat to wildlife in the river.
sentences.fr: La pollution représente une grave menace pour la faune de la rivière.

sentences.en: Bear in mind that the museum closes early on Sundays.
sentences.fr: Garde à l'esprit que le musée ferme tôt le dimanche.

sentences.en: It took Dad years to come to terms with his team's defeat.
sentences.fr: Il a fallu des années à papa pour accepter la défaite de son équipe.

sentences.en: We shouldn't draw any conclusions before we have all the facts.
sentences.fr: Nous ne devrions tirer aucune conclusion avant d'avoir tous les faits.

sentences.en: The teacher made allowances for Noah because he had been sick.
sentences.fr: L'enseignante a été indulgente avec Noah parce qu'il avait été malade.

sentences.en: After hours of arguing, the twins reached a compromise.
sentences.fr: Après des heures de dispute, les jumeaux ont trouvé un compromis.

grammar.q: Will we have homework this weekend? ___
grammar.explain: « J'espère que non » = I hope not. Not remplace toute la proposition négative.

grammar.q: I don't like these sunglasses. Do you have any cheaper ___?
grammar.explain: Sunglasses est pluriel et dénombrable : on le remplace par ones (cheaper ones).

grammar.q: Wildfires ___ a serious threat to many small towns.
grammar.explain: La collocation est pose a threat (représenter une menace). Make a threat veut dire menacer quelqu'un.

grammar.q: Comment dit-on « Je pense que oui » ?
grammar.explain: Après think, so remplace la proposition positive : I think so. Jamais I think yes.

grammar.q: If we don't ___ the deadline, our project won't be accepted.
grammar.explain: On dit meet a deadline. Respect a deadline est un calque du français.

grammar.q: Is the swimming pool closed today? ___ They're cleaning it.
grammar.explain: La piscine EST fermée (mauvaise nouvelle) : I'm afraid so = malheureusement oui.

grammar.q: Is the ferry still running? I'm afraid ___. It stopped last week.
grammar.explain: Le traversier ne fonctionne plus : I'm afraid not = malheureusement non.

grammar.q: If you need to leave early, please ___ quietly.
grammar.explain: Do so remplace l'action déjà mentionnée (leave early) dans un registre soutenu.

grammar.q: My old phone kept freezing, so I bought a new ___.
grammar.explain: Phone est singulier et dénombrable : on le remplace par one (a new one).

grammar.q: You should ___ in mind that the roads may be icy.
grammar.explain: Bear in mind (ou keep in mind) = garder à l'esprit.

grammar.q: It took Zoé months to ___ terms with moving to a new city.
grammar.explain: Come to terms with = accepter une situation difficile.

grammar.q: What conclusion can we ___ from these results?
grammar.explain: On tire une conclusion : draw a conclusion, jamais take ni pull.

grammar.q: Would you like to come skating with us? I'd love ___!
grammar.explain: To seul remplace to come skating : I'd love to. Sans to, la réponse est incomplète.

grammar.q: Will Grandpa like the gift? I think yes.
grammar.explain: « Je pense que oui » = I think so, jamais I think yes.

grammar.q: I lost my mittens, so Mom bought me new one.
grammar.explain: Mittens est pluriel : on le remplace par ones (new ones).

grammar.q: Climate change makes a serious threat to polar bears.
grammar.explain: La collocation est pose a threat to : Climate change poses a serious threat.

grammar.q: Is the math test cancelled? I'm afraid no.
grammar.explain: Après I'm afraid, on dit not (ou so), jamais no.

grammar.q: The old diary sheds light in the history of our town.
grammar.explain: La collocation est shed light on (faire la lumière sur), avec on.

reading.title: The Raccoon Summit
reading.text:
Last Thursday, the residents of Maple Street held an emergency meeting at the community centre. The subject? A raccoon named Bandit, who had been raiding their green bins for weeks.

Mrs. Leblanc spoke first. "This animal poses a serious threat to our neighbourhood," she declared. "Will he stop on his own? I very much doubt it." Mr. Chen disagreed. "Bear in mind that Bandit was here long before we were," he said. "We should learn to live with him, not fight him."

Young Sofia, who had been taking notes, raised her hand. "Before we draw any conclusions, shouldn't we take into account why he keeps coming back?" Everyone turned to look at her. "Our bins are full of pizza crusts. If I were a raccoon, I would come too." Some neighbours laughed; others did not.

After an hour of arguing, the residents finally reached a compromise. Each family would buy a raccoon-proof bin, and anyone who wished to keep feeding the birds could do so, but only in the morning. Mrs. Leblanc was not entirely satisfied. "Will this really work?" she asked. "I hope so," replied Mr. Chen. "If it doesn't, we'll have to come to terms with our furry neighbour."

The new bins arrived on Monday. On Tuesday, Bandit inspected them carefully. On Wednesday, he tried to open one, and on Thursday he tried again, this time with two of his friends. By Friday, the whole street was holding its breath.

Have the bins defeated him? So far, they have. Bandit now spends his nights on Elm Street, where nobody has bought new bins yet. The residents of Elm Street have called a meeting for next Thursday. Sofia has offered to share her notes. They will probably need them.

questions.q: Why did the residents of Maple Street hold a meeting?
choices: Because a raccoon kept getting into their bins
Because the city had stopped collecting garbage
To choose a name for a new pet

questions.q: What did Mr. Chen mean by "Bear in mind that Bandit was here long before we were"?
choices: Bandit is a very old raccoon.
People should remember that the raccoon lived there first.
Bandit had been living in Mr. Chen's house.
The residents had forgotten about the meeting.

questions.q: In the compromise, what does "could do so" refer to?

choices: The raccoon comes back because there is food in the bins.
The residents should buy pizza for the raccoon.

questions.q: In the last paragraph, what does "So far, they have" mean?
choices: The bins have not arrived yet.
The raccoons have opened the bins.
Up to now, the bins have stopped Bandit.
The residents have bought more bins.

questions.q: Why will the residents of Elm Street probably need Sofia's notes?
choices: Because Sofia is moving to Elm Street
Because they now have the same raccoon problem
Because they want to write a book about Bandit
Because their meeting will be in French

pron.focus: L'auxiliaire qui reste seul est fort
pron.explain: Dans une phrase normale, les petits mots comme [[can]], [[do]] ou [[to]] sont faibles : « keun », « deu », « teu ». Mais quand l'ellipse les laisse **seuls en fin de phrase**, ils reprennent leur son **plein** : [[but my sister can]] se dit « KANN », jamais « keun » ; [[I'd love to]] finit par un « tou » bien net. Dans [[I hope so]] et [[I'm afraid not]], l'accent tombe sur le verbe, puis [[so]] ou [[not]] se pose clairement. Et dans [[the blue one]], c'est la couleur qu'on accentue : [[one]] reste léger.

words.hint: « aï-HÔP-sô » : accent sur HOPE, so bien rond
« aïm-eu-FRÉÏD-NOT » : not bien net à la fin
« if-iou-WANT-tou » : le to final garde un « ou » plein
« dzeu-BLOU-ouann » : accent sur la couleur, one léger

Will it snow tomorrow? I'm afraid so.
I don't want the red one, I want the blue one.

mission.prompt: Ton oncle t'appelle : il veut savoir si tu viens au chalet en fin de semaine, s'il va neiger et si tu peux apporter ses vieilles raquettes. Réponds-lui (cinq à huit phrases) sans répéter les verbes : so / not, un auxiliaire seul, one / ones, do so, et au moins deux collocations de la leçon.
mission.model: Am I coming to the cottage this weekend? I hope so! Will it snow? I'm afraid not, but bear in mind that the weather can change quickly up north. Your old snowshoes are broken, so I'll bring my new ones instead. Mom can't come, but Dad can. He wants to drive, and if the roads are icy, he'll do so very carefully. Don't worry, we'll take into account that you go to bed early!
checklist: J'ai répondu avec [[I hope so]] ou [[I'm afraid not]], sans [[I hope yes]] ni [[I think no]]
J'ai repris un auxiliaire seul ([[Dad can]]) au lieu de répéter le verbe, et je l'ai prononcé fort
J'ai remplacé un nom par [[one]] ou [[ones]]
J'ai utilisé [[do so]] ou une ellipse avec [[to]]
J'ai placé au moins deux collocations ([[bear in mind]], [[take into account]]…)
